description: Assemble the full left Aero Hand in the live preview: attach every finger (thumb plus 4 fingers) from the existing STLs at their correct joints and poses, as separable parts, and use that full-hand model in the reBot arm mount design. Jake: "Attach all the fingers to the Aero Hand. Since we have those STL files, we might as well." Today the Base 10/11 preview (gripper.scad aero_hand(), export_models.py REFS) shows only the palm, left_base_link.STL; the finger link meshes are in third_party/aero_hand/guide/anim41/left_*_link.STL (joint origins in the Aero Hand URDF). Follows voice-3cd78d20.

results.identified_issue: Base 13 copies v311 (not v312) because the Aero Hand only appears with motor_sts 0 (RS00 + wrist mount), which Base 12 removed. Hand parts are written by numpy (hand_pose.py imports arm_pose's frame/axis_rot/read_stl/write_stl) into exports/parts/aero_*.stl at the origin gripper.scad echoes for part=viewer_aero_plate (aero_view_x,0,tool_z+aero_spacer); gripper.scad's aero_hand() now imports those STLs, so they must exist before OpenSCAD previews — export_models.main() runs arm() and hand() first. The REFS palm part (viewer_aero_hand) was removed. Joint mapping: curl -> index..pinky mcp_flex/pip/dip + thumb mcp/ip; thumb_abd -> left_thumb_cmc_abd; thumb_flex -> left_thumb_cmc_flex; clamped to URDF limits. Verified visually only (renders at several poses); export_models/genus/check_geometry all pass. Scripts/test_gripper_poses.py has one pre-existing failure (v306 has no poses.js entry), unrelated. Hand STLs total ~4 MB (guide meshes, not decimated).
results.summary: Base 13: the Aero Hand now has all five fingers (thumb + index, middle, ring, pinky), each a separate part, posed from its URDF beside the arm
results.detailed_description:
The Aero Hand in the arm-mount design is now the whole left hand, not just the palm. A small script (third_party/aero_hand/hand_pose.py) reads the hand's URDF and places every finger link STL at its real joint, using the same forward-kinematics helpers as the arm poser. It writes six separate parts — palm, thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky — so each shows as its own model in the live preview and explodes apart.

It's a new version, Base 13 (v313_generalist_aero_full_hand): Base 11 set to the RS00 motor, so the reBot wrist mount and arm are shown. No printed part changes. Base 12 isn't the base for it because Base 12 dropped the RS00 and the arm mount.

The pose is three new Tune sliders under 'Aero Hand plate': finger curl (default 15°), thumb abduction (45°), and thumb flex (10°). Together they give a relaxed open hand, and the live preview re-poses the hand as you drag them. One limit to know about: a single curl angle drives every finger joint. On the real hand the tendons couple the joints, so the poses are illustrative, not exact.

I also fixed a fresh-checkout problem: the arm and hand STLs are now written before the previews that import them. The first run had rendered arm_view without the arm. The Tune view also keeps the arm now (live_render copies its STLs); Base 10/11 dropped it there.

summary: The live preview of the Aero Hand in gripper.scad aero_hand() shows only the palm, so the thumb and four finger meshes are missing. Attach every finger from the existing STLs at its URDF joint pose as separable parts, and use that full hand in the reBot arm mount design.
